The vector noise uses offset inputs $(\pm 0.1)$ to ensure the three components are not identical, creating a 3D vector field [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the pseudo-code and algorithm steps that the 3D vector noise is calculated by sampling the fBm function at three different offsets: the original coordinates (xsphere, ysphere, zsphere), coordinates offset by +0.1, and coordinates offset by -0.1. This technique is standard in procedural generation to ensure the noise values for the X, Y, and Z components are not identical (which would happen if the same input were used for all three), thereby creating a proper 3D vector field.
